title: Reel Studio: type an idea, get a video

scenes.headline: Type an idea. Get a video.
scenes.narration: Type an idea. Get a finished video.

scenes.headline: On your own computer
scenes.narration: Reel Studio makes short videos and podcasts on your own computer. No account, no cloud render, and no fee per video.

scenes.headline: How it works
scenes.narration: A storyboard describes the video. Reel Studio does the rest: the voice, the scenes, the captions, the music, and the final MP4.
items: Voice, scenes, captions and music are made here

scenes.headline: One small JSON file
scenes.narration: The only step that needs AI is writing that storyboard, and it is just a small JSON file. Write it yourself, ask a model that runs on your machine, or let your coding agent do it.

scenes.headline: A scene in the storyboard
scenes.narration: Each scene says what to show and what to say. That is all the model has to write.

scenes.headline: Or let your agent do it
scenes.narration: Or give it to your coding agent through MCP. One command adds the server, and the agent can make videos on its own.

code.text:
$ claude mcp add reel-studio -- node bin/reel-studio.mjs mcp
agent> create_video "Why the sky is blue"
queued job
succeeded

scenes.headline: Cloud tools or Reel Studio
scenes.narration: Cloud video tools charge per video and upload your content. Reel Studio is free, stays on your machine, and gives the same video from the same storyboard.

left.label: Cloud video tools
left.text: Credits per video, your content uploaded

right.label: Reel Studio
right.text: Free, local, the same video every time

scenes.headline: What you get
scenes.narration: You get a local voice, captions you can edit, portrait, landscape or square, and two-host podcasts.

scenes.headline: What it is not
scenes.narration: It is made for motion graphics: text, charts, lists and code. It does not make talking avatars or generated footage, and it says so.

scenes.headline: Free and open source
scenes.narration: Reel Studio is free and open source. Clone it, make your first video, and tell us what broke.
